title: FIPS operational risk: require_fips check uses re-read fips_provider_loaded after lookup, not provider identity
description: In ioctl_init (crypto2dev_fd.c ~line 760), REQUIRE_FIPS is enforced by calling crypto2dev_fips_provider_loaded() *after* crypto2dev_lookup_algo() has already selected and ref-counted a provider. The lookup and the REQUIRE_FIPS check are two separate atomic reads of fips_provider_count with no lock held across them. Race: (1) REQUIRE_FIPS set, (2) INIT called while fips_provider_count=0 so lookup selects kcapi ops, (3) wolfssl provider loads between lookup and the require_fips check, (4) fips_provider_loaded() returns true, require_fips check passes, session proceeds with non-FIPS kcapi ops. Even without the race, the check is semantically wrong: it asks 'is any FIPS provider loaded?' not 'did this lookup select a FIPS provider?'. A correct implementation checks whether the returned provider's is_fips==1, not whether fips_provider_loaded() is true. Consequence: a caller that issues REQUIRE_FIPS to guarantee FIPS-validated crypto could get a non-FIPS session without any error — silent FIPS bypass under a narrow but real TOCTOU window. At CMVP audit time this is a material nonconformance.
